Second-generation bulk RNA-seq deconvolution algorithms

Source: vignettes/deconvolution_description.qmd

Deconvolution algorithms included in the benchmark

Note

Shared notation: Y = \((Y_{gn}) \in \mathbb{R}^{G \times N}\) is the bulk matrix; X = \((X_{gj}) \in \mathbb{R}^{G \times J}\) is the single-cell or purified reference matrix; P = \((P_{jn}) \in \mathbb{R}^{J \times N}\) is the cell-type proportion matrix. The generic convolution model is \[ \mathbf{Y} \approx \mathbf{X}\mathbf{P} + \mathbf{E}, \qquad \mathbf{1}^{\top}\mathbf{p}_n=1,\quad \mathbf{p}_n \geq 0. \]

See Table 1.

Benchmarking metrics

We compare in Table 2 the following metrics for cellular composition deconvolution, where the true composition is \(p=(p_1,\dots,p_J)\) and the estimated composition is \(\hat p=(\hat p_1,\dots,\hat p_J)\), with \(p_j,\hat p_j\in[0,1]\) and \(\sum_j p_j=\sum_j \hat p_j=1\). Note that the Aitchison distance, and the Jensen Shannon divergence are grounded in compositional-data geometry, while the RMSE, MAE, and Pearson correlation are commonly used in most regression frameworks.
